Hi Kim,

Thanks again for taking this on. Per our call earlier this week, I attached 7 days of anonymized usage (hawthorn_usage_samples.csv) with request timestamps, prompt token counts, and generated token counts. High-level notes:
- Peak observed requests: ~480 RPS over a 20-minute window (on 2026-07-06).
- Average prompt tokens: 160; average generated tokens: 90 (so ~250 tokens per request on average).
- Typical workload: mix of chat completions (80%) and single-turn generation (20%).
- SLO target: p95 end-to-end latency <= 400ms for the interactive chat flows.

Can you map that to tokens/sec and give a recommendation for a Dedicated slab size with headroom for 30% burst and a canary plan? Also please note any assumptions about model variants and batching impact.

We’re hoping to get a firm committed proposal for procurement next week. Procurement contact is procurement@hawthorn.ai — looping them in for visibility.

Appreciate it — Hannah

From: kimberly_park@redwood.ai
To: Hannah Lee <hannah.lee@hawthorn.ai>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 19 Jul 2026 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity sizing request — sample usage attached

Hannah — thanks for the data, that’s exactly what we need to produce a commit recommendation. A few clarifying Qs before I run full modeling:
1) Is the 480 RPS peak synchronous (all users awaiting responses) or measured as inbound request rate while clients accept async responses?
2) Are you planning to use a single model family (e.g., Llama-3-16B quantized) in production, or will you route to smaller fallbacks for cheap, low-latency flows?
3) Do you expect a steady growth curve (10–20% month-over-month) or large one-off spikes from seasonal events?

Quick back-of-envelope mapping based on the CSV:
- Peak RPS (observed): 480 RPS
- Avg tokens/request: 250 tokens
- Peak tokens/sec = 480 * 250 = 120,000 tokens/sec at ingress

Assumptions for a practical Dedicated recommendation:
- Model baseline: Llama-3-16B (4-bit quantized) — gives ~6,000 tokens/sec per A100-80 GPU under our continuous-batching runtime for typical 2–4k context windows.
- Effective per-GPU throughput (real-world, accounting for KV cache multiples and tail latency constraints): conservatively 5,500 tokens/sec.

Simple math: 120,000 / 5,500 = 21.8 → round up to 22 GPUs.
Add 30% burst/headroom for traffic spikes and canary windows: 22 * 1.30 = 28.6 → recommend a 29-GPU slab as a single committed unit.

SLO notes (p95 <= 400ms): achieving this at peak depends on batching strategy and cold-cache behavior. With Dedicated and our KV prefix caching enabled, steady-state p95 should be achievable on the 16–20 GPU range; the additional headroom covers burst spikes and rolling upgrades.

I’ll create a detailed model workbook with breakdowns per-request-type, alternate model flavors (smaller model fallback and 70B variant for higher-quality paths), and an ops playbook for graceful fallback. Looping Ben for procurement/discount guidance on a 12-month commit.

Thanks — Kim
Director, Strategic Accounts, Redwood Inference

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
To: kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 20 Jul 2026 11:10:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Dedicated capacity sizing request — technical validation

Kim / Ben — forwarding my engineering validation after reviewing Hannah’s CSV and Kim’s BOE. Key technical caveats and recommendations:

> On Mon, Jul 19, 2026 at 09:22 AM kimberly_park@redwood.ai wrote:
> > Quick back-of-envelope mapping based on the CSV:
> > - Peak RPS (observed): 480 RPS
> > - Avg tokens/request: 250 tokens
> > - Peak tokens/sec = 480 * 250 = 120,000 tokens/sec at ingress
> >
> > Assumptions for a practical Dedicated recommendation:
> > - Model baseline: Llama-3-16B (4-bit quantized) — gives ~6,000 tokens/sec per A100-80 GPU under our continuous-batching runtime for typical 2–4k context windows.

Technical validation and variables that materially change GPU count:
- Batching efficiency: If the traffic is highly spiky (many tiny bursts) our effective per-GPU throughput will drop (we model 4k–5.5k tokens/sec/GPU under poor batching). If you can buffer 50–100ms at the edge we typically regain batching efficiency.
- KV cache hit-rate: For chat workloads we assume ~40% prefix reuse; higher reuse can double effective tokens/sec for interactive flows. Please confirm how often users reference prior turns vs starting fresh threads.
- Cold vs warm: cold starts (cache miss + model loading) introduce large p95 outliers; Dedicated avoids host-level swapping but model reloads during upgrades still cost. We recommend 2x redundancy per availability zone for rolling upgrades.
- Model choice: Llama-3-70B for higher quality will reduce tokens/sec per GPU by ~3–4x; a mixed fleet (16B for fast paths, 70B on demand) is often the best trade.

Recommendation: define a committed slab sized to cover 75–80% of expected peak steady-state (16–18 GPUs), paired with a burst buffer (on-demand / reserved spare GPUs) to 28–30 GPUs for 30% headroom. Operationally easier for us to provision a 24 GPU reserved slab plus a 6–8 GPU burst pool (total 30) so you get predictable base throughput and clear entitlement for spikes.

I attached an initial workbook (hawthorn_commit_model.xlsx) with three scenarios (conservative, baseline, aggressive) and per-GPU cost estimates.

Karthik
Senior Systems Engineer, Redwood Inference
[attachment: hawthorn_commit_model.xlsx (xlsx)]

Subject: Redwood Dedicated proposal — recommended sizing & next steps (HAW-2331)

Hannah / Marcus / Procurement — following the data review and engineering validation, here’s a concise recommendation and next steps so procurement can action quickly.

Summary recommendation
- Recommended committed slab: 24 x A100-80 GPUs (Redwood Dedicated, single region, multi-AZ placement).
- Burst buffer: 6–8 GPUs available as a soft reserve for 30% headroom (auto-burst).
- Total entitlement during bursts: up to 30–32 GPUs.
- Rationale: balances steady-state throughput to cover ~80% of observed peak (480 RPS) while keeping a modest, reliable burst pool for traffic variance and rolling upgrades.

Modeling highlights (baseline scenario)
- Baseline tokens/sec demand (observed peak): 120k tokens/sec
- Effective throughput per A100-80 (Llama-3-16B, production tuning): ~5.5k tokens/sec → 120k/5.5k = 21.8 GPUs → round to 22 for coverage
- Safety + ops buffers → recommend 24 committed GPUs with 6–8 burst GPUs for a comfortable 30% headroom and redundancy for upgrades
- p95 latency target (<= 400ms): expected to pass in steady-state with our batching and KV caching enabled; recommend load-test and a 2-week canary before traffic migration

Commercial and next steps
1) I’m proposing a 12-month commitment on a 24 GPU slab + 6 GPU burst pool. Ben, can you confirm discount tiers and ship a term sheet?
2) Procurement — if OK, please review the attached proposal (redwood_dedicated_proposal.pdf) and confirm a PO contact / billing entity.
3) Technical: schedule a 60-minute runbook & canary planning session with Karthik and our SRE team — I propose Thu 2026-07-29 08:00–09:00 PT.

Action items
- Hawthorn: confirm whether you want a mixed-model routing strategy (16B baseline + 70B fallback) or single-model rollout.
- Procurement: share PO contact and desired billing cadence.
- Redwood: Ben to send pricing/term sheet; Karthik to prepare canary checklist.

I’ve attached the workbook and the proposal PDF for procurement. Happy to jump on a quick sync to walk through the numbers.

— Kim
Director, Strategic Accounts, Redwood Inference
